title: Cohomology of the base change map through the Kunneth identification
statement:
Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed], let $n\geq1$ be an integer invertible in $K$, and put $A=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$. Let $j:U\to X$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] of schemes of finite type over $K$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $Y$ be projective over $K$ [def-kun-projective], and let $F$ be a sheaf of $A$-modules on $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, viewed in degree zero in the ordinary module derived category [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Put $Z=Y\times_KX$ and $W=Y\times_KU$ [def-pc-fibre-product], with projections $r:Z\to Y$, $q:Z\to X$, $s:W\to Y$, $p:W\to U$, and $h=1_Y\times j:W\to Z$. Thus $qh=jp$ and $rh=s$.

Write $\Ex:q^{-1}Rj_*F\to Rh_*p^{-1}F$ for the exchange of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. All tensor products below are derived over $A$ [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Let $E=\underline A_Y$ [def-kun-constant-sheaf]. The external-product maps of [def-kun-kunneth-map], with the pullback-of-constant and tensor-unit identifications, give the Kunneth isomorphisms [lem-kun-0f14b]
$$
 k_Z:R\Gamma(Y,E)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R\Gamma(X,Rj_*F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(Z,q^{-1}Rj_*F),
$$
$$
 k_W:R\Gamma(Y,E)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R\Gamma(U,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(W,p^{-1}F).
$$
Let $\lambda_j:R\Gamma(X,Rj_*F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(U,F)$ and $\lambda_h:R\Gamma(Z,Rh_*p^{-1}F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(W,p^{-1}F)$ be the canonical module-valued Leray comparisons: the inverses of the derived direct-image composition comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], normalized by the composite adjunction as in [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition]. Then
$$
 \lambda_h\circ R\Gamma(Z,\Ex)\circ k_Z
 =k_W\circ(1_{R\Gamma(Y,E)}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\lambda_j).
$$
Equivalently, under these two Kunneth identifications and the Leray identifications, $R\Gamma(Z,\Ex)$ is the identity of $R\Gamma(Y,\underline A_Y)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R\Gamma(U,F)$.

proof.text: Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}K$. The point category causes no change of coefficients. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product] and [def-kun-separably-closed] say that each affine scheme etale over $K$ is a finite disjoint union of copies of $S$. Such affine opens cover every etale $K$-scheme; its points are open copies of $S$. The sheaf axiom therefore identifies a sheaf on $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ with the rule $V\mapsto M^{\pi_0(V)}$, where $M$ is its value at $S$, and morphisms with maps of $M$. For module sheaves take $M$ an $A$-module, with every operation componentwise. Evaluation at $S$ and the constant-sheaf functor are thus inverse exact equivalences between $A$-module sheaves on $S_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $A$-modules. Their tensor comparison is the identity at $S$, hence is an isomorphism of sheaves; termwise application gives the corresponding equivalence of derived categories. We may consequently write $Ra_{T*}=R\Gamma(T,-)$ for a structure map $a_T:T\to S$. This is an identification of module categories, not forgetting the $A$-action.

source.place: Tag 00U3, label lemma-etale-over-field; elementary sheaf-gluing specialization to a separably closed field

proof.text:
Write $a:Y\to S$, $b:X\to S$, $c=bj:U\to S$, $d=bq:Z\to S$, and $e=dh=cp:W\to S$. Set $H=Rj_*F$, $P=Ra_*E$, $B=Rb_*H$, and $C=Rc_*F$. Use the inverse composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] for $(j,b)$ and $(h,d)$ to define $\lambda_j:B\to C$ and $\lambda_h:Rd_*Rh_*p^{-1}F\to Re_*p^{-1}F$. The sites may be replaced by small representatives in a larger universe; the ring on each is the constant $A$, and the structural ring maps are the pullback-of-constant isomorphisms. All derived inverse-image/direct-image adjunctions are those fixed by [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. The normalization in the composition statement agrees with the right-adjoint comparison as follows. For either inner map $f=j$ or $f=h$, if $I$ is K-injective, then $f_*I$ is K-injective: for an acyclic complex $N$, the adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(N,f_*I)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(f^{-1}N,I)$, which is acyclic because $f^{-1}$ is exact. Thus in the normalization one may take $J=f_*I$ and the resolution map to be the identity. On these representatives, the comparison is the ordinary direct-image composition identification and its adjunction is the composite of the two ordinary Hom bijections. Consequently [lem-cat-right-adjoint-composition] identifies its counit with the pasted counit. Naturality of the resolution identifications gives this normalization for every derived object. With the canonical inverse-image composition identifications understood, this gives the two typed identities
$$
 \varepsilon_{c,F}\circ c^{-1}(\lambda_j)
 =\varepsilon_{j,F}\circ j^{-1}(\varepsilon_{b,H})
 :c^{-1}B\longrightarrow F,
$$
$$
 \varepsilon_{e,p^{-1}F}\circ e^{-1}(\lambda_h)
 =\varepsilon_{h,p^{-1}F}\circ h^{-1}(\varepsilon_{d,Rh_*p^{-1}F}).
$$
These formulas fix the actual Leray maps and their directions, not just isomorphisms of their endpoints.

proof.text:
By [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper], $Y$ is proper over $K$. Thus [lem-kun-0f14b] applies to $(Y,X,E,H)$ and $(Y,U,E,F)$: $K$ is separably closed, $n$ is invertible, $X$ and $U$ are finite type, and both $H$ and $F$ belong to the stated unbounded $A$-module categories. No constructibility or separatedness of $X$ is required. By [lem-kun-pullback-constant], $r^{-1}E=A_Z$ and $s^{-1}E=A_W$ canonically. The left unit constraints of [lem-kun-tensor-unit] therefore give isomorphisms
$$u_Z:r^{-1}E\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}q^{-1}H\to q^{-1}H,
\qquad u_W:s^{-1}E\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}p^{-1}F\to p^{-1}F.$$
In the notation of [def-kun-kunneth-map], the maps in the statement are precisely $k_Z=Rd_*(u_Z)\circ\kappa_{E,H}$ and $k_W=Re_*(u_W)\circ\kappa_{E,F}$. Both are invertible. The current definition fixes the comparison
$$
 t_Z=(\gamma_{a,r,P}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\gamma_{b,q,B})\circ(\mu^d_{P,B})^{-1}
 :d^{-1}(P\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B)\longrightarrow r^{-1}a^{-1}P\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}q^{-1}b^{-1}B.
$$
Here $\gamma_{a,r}:d^{-1}\to r^{-1}a^{-1}$ and $\gamma_{b,q}:d^{-1}\to q^{-1}b^{-1}$ are exactly its termwise-descended constant-coefficient module composition maps. Thus the transpose of $k_Z$ is
$$u_Z\circ(r^{-1}\varepsilon_{a,E}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}q^{-1}\varepsilon_{b,H})\circ t_Z.$$
For any $L,M\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ put
$$t_W(L,M)=(\gamma_{a,s,L}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}\gamma_{c,p,M})\circ(\mu^e_{L,M})^{-1}.
$$
The transpose of $k_W$ is
$$u_W\circ(s^{-1}\varepsilon_{a,E}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}p^{-1}\varepsilon_{c,F})\circ t_W(P,C).$$ These are the maps obtained from the definition's explicit unit-then-direct-image formula for $\kappa$, under its canonical K-injective Hom bijection.

proof.text:
Let $D=P\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$. We compare the two asserted maps $D\to Re_*p^{-1}F$ under the bijection $\operatorname{Hom}(D,Re_*p^{-1}F)=\operatorname{Hom}(e^{-1}D,p^{-1}F)$. By [def-kun-kunneth-map], the adjoint of $k_Z$ is $u_Z\circ(r^{-1}\varepsilon_{a,E}\otimes q^{-1}\varepsilon_{b,H})\circ t_Z$, with $t_Z$ fixed in step 3. By [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], $\varepsilon_h\circ h^{-1}\Ex=p^{-1}\varepsilon_{j,F}$, after the specified square comparison. Use the second counit identity in step 2 and naturality of $\varepsilon_d$ to transpose the left side. It is exactly
$$
 e^{-1}(P\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B)
 \cong s^{-1}a^{-1}P\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}p^{-1}j^{-1}b^{-1}B
 \xrightarrow{\ s^{-1}\varepsilon_{a,E}\otimes p^{-1}j^{-1}\varepsilon_{b,H}\ }
 s^{-1}E\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}p^{-1}j^{-1}H
 \xrightarrow{\ 1\otimes p^{-1}\varepsilon_{j,F}\ }
 s^{-1}E\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}p^{-1}F
 \xrightarrow{u_W}p^{-1}F.
$$
For clarity, the naturality used here is
$\varepsilon_{d,Rh_*p^{-1}F}\circ d^{-1}Rd_*(\Ex)=\Ex\circ\varepsilon_{d,q^{-1}H}$; the equality for the adjoint of $\Ex$ then removes $h^{-1}\Ex$. Thus the outer Leray comparison is accounted for explicitly. On the right side, the adjoint of $k_W\circ(1_P\otimes\lambda_j)$ is
$$
u_W\circ(s^{-1}\varepsilon_{a,E}\otimes p^{-1}\varepsilon_{c,F})
\circ t_W(P,C)\circ e^{-1}(1_P\otimes\lambda_j).
$$
Naturality of $\mu^e$ and $\gamma_{c,p}$ gives the typed equality
$$
t_W(P,C)\circ e^{-1}(1_P\otimes\lambda_j)
=(1_{s^{-1}a^{-1}P}\otimes p^{-1}c^{-1}\lambda_j)\circ t_W(P,B).
$$
Thus this adjoint equals
$$
u_W\circ\bigl(s^{-1}\varepsilon_{a,E}\otimes
p^{-1}(\varepsilon_{c,F}\circ c^{-1}\lambda_j)\bigr)\circ t_W(P,B).
$$
Substitute the first counit identity from step 2. Bifunctoriality of tensor makes this exactly the preceding three-arrow composite, with the comparisons checked in step 4. Injectivity of the adjunction bijection proves the displayed equality in the statement. This calculation uses only the adjoint descriptions and pasted counits, not a base-change isomorphism theorem.

proof.text:
The common source can now be identified with $P\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C$ by $1_P\otimes\lambda_j$. The equality of step 5 reads
$$k_W^{-1}\circ\lambda_h\circ R\Gamma(Z,\Ex)\circ k_Z\circ(1_P\otimes\lambda_j)^{-1}=1_{P\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C}.$$
Every inverse exists by steps 2 and 3. This is the claimed identity on $R\Gamma(Y,\underline A_Y)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}R\Gamma(U,F)$.
